claims.text: The initial and baseline material is single-phase fcc FeCoNi.
Al and Cu are non-magnetic elements suitable for the proposed addition.
Adding 0-5 at% of the non-magnetic element can preserve a single-phase fcc structure.
Adding a small amount of Al or Cu to single-phase fcc FeCoNi reduces its magnetic anisotropy.
Adding a small amount of Al or Cu to single-phase fcc FeCoNi reduces its exchange bias.
Decreased magnetic anisotropy leads to a reduced coercive field.
Decreased exchange bias leads to a reduced coercive field.
The non-magnetic-element addition will increase coercive field relative to single-phase fcc FeCoNi.
Introducing a small amount of Al or Cu can overcome the coercivity limitation of single-phase fcc FeCoNi.
The proposed comparison is bounded to room-temperature magnetic measurements.

contradictions.description: The mechanism explicitly predicts reduced coercive field, whereas the predicted outcome requires increased coercive field.
The hypothesis says the low-coercivity limitation is overcome by reducing anisotropy and exchange bias, but its own mechanism states that these reductions further reduce coercivity.

The condition specifies no external magnetic field, whereas determining a coercive field ordinarily requires an applied-field hysteresis measurement; the intended distinction between treatment conditions and measurement conditions is not stated.
